input:
We're seeing intermittent L2 ECC correctable errors on Cortex-X925 cores in our ARM CSS v2 cluster under sustained compute load. The kernel log shows:

  [  142.381204] EDAC MC0: 1 CE L2 ECC error on CPU4 (location: set=0x1f way=0x3 bank=0x0)
  [  142.381291] EDAC MC0: total module reports: CE: 12 UE: 0

The X925 runs at 3.2 GHz on a 0.85 V rail. Thermal sensor on the big-core cluster reads 87°C at time of event. DVFS is in use with schedutil governor. I suspect the L2 SRAM is marginal at high voltage-temperature combinations, but I'm not sure whether this is a timing margin issue, a power noise problem on the core VDD rail, or a silicon defect. What diagnostic steps should I take to distinguish these causes, and which ARM CSS v2 RAS registers should I read to get more fault detail?
